evidence: CDIAL 9500 *bhiyagna wet explicitly gives Oriya bhigā and the bhig- verb family, distinguishing the g-bearing stem from *bhiyajyate 9502. The simple bhig/big wet responses preserve that stem, with regional l-participial endings, aspiration and inflection qualified. No underlying nasal is supplied where the survey has none; the precise local transmission remains unresolved.

CDIAL 9502 *bhiyajyate gets wet explicitly gives Assamese bhiziba, Bengali bhijā, Oriya bhijibā, Maithili bhijlāh wet and Bhojpuri bhījal. The survey bij/bhij/bhiz series and l-participial forms match those comparanda. Affricate/retroflex-affricate notation, aspiration, final vowels and local transmission remain qualified; no extra light verb is silently discarded.

CDIAL 5812 *tinta wet explicitly gives Assamese/Bengali titā, Maithili tital/tītal wet and Hindi tītā. Simple tit/tital responses fit this family; vowel and l-inflection variation is retained and local transmission unresolved. Retroflex ṭiṭino and voiced-d extensions are not included here.

CDIAL 9503 *bhiyañjati wets/is wetted explicitly gives Bhojpuri bhī̃jal and Gujarati bhĩjāvũ/bhĩjavvũ. Nasal binj/bhinj wet responses match this nasal branch, with aspiration loss, y/ai and l-participial endings qualified. They are not collapsed into the nonnasal 9502 stem; the local transmission route remains open.
